title: Etale pullback and ringed chart localization for algebraic spaces
statement: Work in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and $h:X\to Y$ a morphism. Use the small etale ringed topoi and their induced morphism $(h_{\mathrm{et}},h^\sharp)$ from [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], and set $\mathcal E_X=\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})$. The small etale site is subcanonical: $h_T(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(W,T)$ is a sheaf for each etale scheme $T\to X$. For every etale algebraic space $T\to Y$, write $h_T(W)=\operatorname{Hom}_Y(W,T)$ on the scheme site. There are canonical isomorphisms $h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}h_T\cong h_{X\times_YT}$ and $(h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)_{\bar x}\cong F_{h\bar x}$ for every sheaf of sets $F$ and geometric point $\bar x$ (a map from the spectrum of an algebraically closed field). For each etale scheme $U\to X$, there is a ringed equivalence $$(\mathcal E_X/h_U,\mathcal O_X\times h_U\to h_U)\simeq(\operatorname{Sh}(U_{\mathrm{et}}),\mathcal O_U),$$ identifying slice restriction with restriction of sheaves and of their structural rings. Given a commutative square $U\xrightarrow{a}V$, $U\to X$, $V\to Y$, $X\xrightarrow{h}Y$ with $U,V$ schemes and both vertical maps etale, let $s:h_U\to h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}h_V$ be the corresponding map. Under these ringed equivalences, the relocalization whose inverse image is $(H\to h_V)\mapsto(h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}H\times_{h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}h_V,s}h_U\to h_U)$ is canonically isomorphic to $(a_{\mathrm{et}},a^\sharp)$. These comparisons are natural under further chart restrictions and respect the structural ring maps.

source.place: Tag 04K2 (lemma-stalk-pullback), Tag 04M5 (lemma-relocalize-morphism-at-schemes), using Tag 04M4 (lemma-relocalize-morphism); section-localize, equation-localize-at-scheme-ringed. Subcanonicality follows by restricting the fppf sheaves defining algebraic spaces.

proof.text: First check subcanonicality, also on the enlarged sites $\mathcal C_A$ used below. A matching family of maps from scheme objects to a space $T$ glues uniquely because $T$ is an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space] (for a scheme $T$, its representable sheaf $h_T$ is an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]), and etale scheme coverings are fppf coverings by [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. The assertion that the glued map is over $A$ follows by the same uniqueness applied to $A$. For a covering by spaces, pull back to scheme charts and then take scheme charts of its members; these are covering refinements by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density]. Glue the maps on these scheme charts as above. They agree on overlaps, so define a natural transformation into $T$ from the covered fppf sheaf: on each scheme test object the images glue uniquely in $T$. Thus the maps descend uniquely. This proves that $\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,T)$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal C_A$ and that its scheme restriction is the stated $h_T$. In particular the scheme site is subcanonical.

On $\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_X$, [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density] supplies finite limits and [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] supplies the covering-preserving finite-limit functor $v_h:T\mapsto X\times_YT$ with its ringed geometric morphism. Step 1 verifies the subcanonical hypotheses. Apply [lem-pur-site-representable-algebraic-pullback] to $v_h$ and the object $T$. Its normalized comparison gives $h_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}h_T\cong h_{X\times_YT}$ after the restriction equivalences of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The naturality in arrows in that comparison is the naturality required here, including when $T$ is not a scheme.

Write $L_{\bar x}(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,T)$ on $\mathcal C_X$. For a set $A$ put $P_{\bar x}(A)(T)=\operatorname{Map}(L_{\bar x}(T),A)$. This is a sheaf: every lift to a covered $T$ lifts to a covering member. Indeed pull the cover back to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, using [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], refine by schemes, taking surjective etale scheme charts of the pulled-back spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] whose composites to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ are etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], as in the refinement clause of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density], and apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift] to this scheme cover of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Matching functions therefore glue by choosing a lift; two choices give a lift to the fibre-product overlap, so matching makes the value independent of the choice. Fibre products exist by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. On the scheme site, there is an explicit natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(G_{\bar x},A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,P_{\bar x}(A))$: send $b$ to $\alpha_W(t)(l)=b([W,l,t])$. Conversely send $\alpha$ to $[W,l,t]\mapsto\alpha_W(t)(l)$; naturality is exactly invariance under every neighbourhood-colimit relation. Thus the stalk functor of [lem-sfb-space-etale-conservative-geometric-points] is left adjoint to the scheme restriction of $P_{\bar x}$. The enlarged-site equivalence transfers this adjunction. The same construction applies to $Y$ and $\bar y=h\bar x$.

source.place: Tags 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), 00YA (lemma-point-site-topos); spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K0 (lemma-stalk-gives-point). Explicit germ adjunction.

proof.text: The direct-image formula in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] gives $(h_*P_{\bar x}(A))(V)=\operatorname{Map}(L_{\bar x}(X\times_YV),A)$. The fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies a lift to $X\times_YV$ over the fixed $\bar x$ with a lift to $V$ over $\bar y$; this is natural in $V$ and $A$. Hence $h_*P_{\bar x}(A)=P_{\bar y}(A)$ up to this canonical natural isomorphism. The adjunctions of step 3 now give $\operatorname{Hom}((h^{-1}F)_{\bar x},A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h^{-1}F,P_{\bar x}(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,h_*P_{\bar x}(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{\bar y},A)$. Evaluating these natural bijections and their inverses at identity maps gives inverse maps $(h^{-1}F)_{\bar x}\cong F_{\bar y}$, naturally in $F$. Transport to the small sites uses [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. The germ formulas in step 3 identify this with the comparison sending a pulled-back germ at a pair of lifts to the original germ at its target lift. Naturality with projections and each algebraic operation makes it compatible with ring operations; applied to $h^\sharp$ it gives the induced stalk-ring map. This proves the stalk clause without citing the node that depends on the present item.

proof.text: For an etale scheme $U\to X$, postcomposition identifies $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U$: an object on the right is a scheme $W\to X$ with a map $W\to U$ over $X$; that map is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], and composition proves the converse. The arrows and covering families are identical. On $(W\to U)$ both rings have value $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ with the same restrictions, by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] with $A=h_U$, a sheaf by step 1. Its fibre formula identifies $\mathcal E_X/h_U$ with sheaves on this slice site and identifies the slice ring with $(W\to U)\mapsto\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Restricting $(F\times h_U\to h_U)$ gives the fibre $F(W)$ over $W\to U$. This proves the required ringed equivalence and the assertion about restriction.

source.place: Tag 04M1 (equation-localize-at-scheme-ringed); sites-modules.tex localization at a sheaf.

proof.text: Set $P=X\times_YV$ with projections $p:P\to X$ and $b:P\to V$, and $c=(U\to X,a):U\to P$. Since $P$ and $U$ are etale over $X$, [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence] makes $c$ etale. Apply [lem-tw-representable-slice-localized-ringed-morphism] to $v_h$ on the enlarged sites and the object $V$; the hypotheses were checked in steps 1 and 2. On localized sites the base-change functor is $V'/V\mapsto(X\times_YV'\to P)$. Under postcomposition identifications from [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization], this is the functor for $b$, since $P\times_VV'\cong X\times_YV'$ by the projection-preserving fibre-product isomorphism. The cited slice comparison therefore identifies the sliced morphism with $b_{\mathrm{et}}$, including its structural map: restrict first to a scheme object $W\to V$, then to a surjective scheme chart $Z\to P\times_VW$. Both adjoint ring maps send $r\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ to its pullback along $Z\to W$. Scheme restriction is fully faithful by [lem-trf-space-enlarged-site-scheme-density], so these equalities determine the map on all objects of the localized enlarged site. Uniqueness of that normalization in [lem-trf-space-enlarged-chart-ringed-morphism] gives equality of the ring maps.

The map $s$ in the question is $h_c:h_U\to h_P$ through the comparison of step 2. The relocalization formula of [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-slice-functoriality] factors it into the slice morphism over $h_V$ followed on the source by restriction along $h_c$. By [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], the ringed morphism for the etale map $c$ is precisely localization. Step 6 identifies the other factor with $b$. Composition, including the structural maps, is the comparison of [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization]. Since $bc=a$, this composite is $(a_{\mathrm{et}},a^\sharp)$. Transport through scheme restriction and step 5 yields exactly the inverse-image formula in the statement.

For further chart restrictions $U'\to U$, $V'\to V$ forming a compatible square, both maps $U'\to X\times_YV$ have the same projections, hence agree. The naturality of the representable comparison of [lem-pur-site-representable-algebraic-pullback] makes this the commutative square of sheaf maps required by [lem-sfb-ringed-topos-slice-functoriality]. Its restriction square and successive-restriction clause give naturality of the relocalizations. In the chart equivalences of step 5 all restriction maps are literal restriction on the same scheme objects. Finally [lem-trf-space-enlarged-ringed-composition-localization] makes the composition comparisons coherent and ring-compatible. Thus the comparisons already constructed respect every further chart restriction and the structural ring maps, as asserted.
